records.subject: Thin-film Li-ion TREC electrode-selection paradigm
records.object: High thermogalvanic cell coefficient, preferably >0.2 mV K−1
records.quote: In this work, a paradigm to guide the design of thin-filmLi-ion-based TREC cells is established via three criteria for electrodeselection.
context_quotes: These requirements were distilled by translating the TRECprinciple into measurable material properties for Li-ion electrodes.More specifically, the identified criteria included a high thermogalvaniccell coefficient preferably exceeding 0.2 mV K-1, a weak dependence of the thermogalvanic coefficient on the lithiationstate, and a favorable balance between the thermogalvanic cell coefficientand electrode kinetics as estimated from the lithiation overpotential.The material properties necessary to assess these criteria can allbe obtained via a previously developed thermogalvanic characterizationmethodology.
records.conditions: Design criterion derived by translating the TREC principle into measurable electrode properties.

records.quote: Here, we report two superabsorbent monolithic polymer hydrogel matrices designed through vessel-templated synthesis, which act as soft host materials for extremely high concentrations of redox-active ions, namely, [Fe(CN)(6)](3-/4-) and Fe2+/3+.
context_quotes: An unoptimized maximum thermogalvanic power density was observed at ca. 95 mW m(-2) (Delta T of 20 K), on par with other reported gelled systems.
records.conditions: Unoptimized; ΔT = 20 K; on par with other reported gelled systems; individual matrix unspecified.

records.subject: Two superabsorbent monolithic polymer hydrogel matrices
records.quote: Here, we report two superabsorbent monolithic polymer hydrogel matrices designed through vessel-templated synthesis, which act as soft host materials for extremely high concentrations of redox-active ions, namely, [Fe(CN)(6)](3-/4-) and Fe2+/3+.
context_quotes: An optimized thermocapacitance density of ca. 220 F cm(-2) was achieved, which is 15-fold higher than the highest previously reported.
records.conditions: Optimized; reported as 15-fold higher than the highest previous value; individual matrix unspecified.

records.subject: Directional freeze-thawing method
